    "Last updated" (English)
    "最終更新" (Japanese)
    "最終更新日" (Japanese - Last updated date)
    In English, "Last updated" is often used as a shorthand for "Last updated date".
    In Japanese, "最終更新" is a bit more like "Last update" (the event), while "最終更新日" is "Last updated date".
    For a privacy policy, "最終更新日" is the standard.

    Let's go.

    *Self-Correction during final thought*: The prompt says "Use です/ます form for polite-formal tone". This is a very strong instruction. If I don't use it, I might be failing a specific test.
    However, "Keep the same formality level as the source text" is also there.
    If I say "最終更新日は2026年5月です", it is a sentence.
    If I say "最終更新日：2026年5月", it is a label.
    The source "Last updated: May 2026" is a label.
    In UI translation, the structure (Label: Value) is more important than the "です/ます" rule, which is usually applied to body text.
    I will provide the label.

    Actually, I'll check if "Last updated" can be "最終更新日".
    Yes.
    "Last updated: May 2026"
    "最終更新日：2026年5月"

    Final decision: 最終更新日：2026年5月.最終更新日：2026年5月
